summary: Masao Abe was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kyoto, Osaka City, and Columbia Universities and UTS, learning under Tanabe, Hisamatsu, Nishitani, Suzuki, Niebuhr, and Tillich. He held professorships at Nara, Kyoto, and Hanazono.

Masao Shizutani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He served as an assistant professor at Josai University and at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, attested in 1974.

Masao Yamaguchi worked in religious studies and Japanology. After studying at Aoyama Gakuin, University of Tokyo, and Tokyo Metropolitan University, he held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1965–1989), University of Shizuoka, and Sapporo University as dean and president.

Masaru Akimoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held a post at Kyoto Women's University, where he is attested as a professor of contemporary society in 2002 and was affiliated in 2015.

Masashi Nagai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned master's and doctoral degrees at Komazawa University. He spent his career at Komazawa University as lecturer (1984), associate professor, professor emeritus (2017), and president (2019).
Masataka Suzuki is a scholar in religious studies and other fields. He studied at Keio University from approximately 1968 to 1977 and later held a post there from around 1992 to 2015.

Masataro Sawayanagi studied at the University of Tokyo (~1885–1888). He later held posts at Tokyo University of Education (~1901–1910), Tohoku University (~1911–1913), Kyushu University (~1913–1914), and Taisho University (~1926–1927).

Masato Kobayashi is a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Kyoto University (~1989–1995) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1995–2000, PhD) under George Cardona, later serving as a research fellow at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2000–2004).

Masatoshi Konishi was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at International Christian University, University of Calcutta, University of Tokyo, and Rikkyo University, and held positions at Hosei University (1971–1984) and Rikkyo University (1984–2003).

Masatoshi Nagatomi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University, Kyoto University, and Harvard University (PhD ~1951–1957) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and was appointed Instructor of Sanskrit at Harvard in 1958.

Masayuki Taira is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology. After studying at Kyoto University (~1970–1979), he held academic posts at Kansai University (~1985–1996), Osaka University (~1996–2017), and Kyoto Tachibana University (~2017–2022).

Massimo Pallottino was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Rome (~1927–1931) and later held academic posts at the University of Cagliari (~1945–1947) and the University of Rome (~1947–1980).
Masumi Mochizuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Minobusan University, serving as a lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001) and as a professor (attested 2015).

Mathieu Boisvert is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Ravindra Panth, and has served as a professor at the Université du Québec à Montréal since 1992.
Matteo Bartoli was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna (~1894–1898) and under Heinrich Hübschmann (~1899–1900). He held a post at the University of Turin from around 1907 to 1946.

Matthew B. Orsborn is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Hong Kong in 2012 under Guang Xing and Y. Karunadasa, and studied under traditional teachers Hsing Yun and Huishang.
Matthew Clark is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at SOAS University of London, earning his PhD between 1999 and 2004, under teachers Daud Ali and George Botterill.

Matthew Immergut is a scholar of religious studies and other fields who studied under Culadasa. He served as an associate professor of sociology at Purchase College, State University of New York, attested in 2011.

Matthew King is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Toronto in 2014 under Frances Garrett, having also studied under Thubten Champa and traditional teacher Khenpo Kunga Sherab.

Matthew R. Sayers is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Joel Peter Brereton and Patrick Olivelle, and held a post at Lebanon Valley College (attested 2013).
